ABSTRACT: We prove Erd\H{o}s's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. More quantitatively, for every fixed $k\ge3$, we show \[ r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp\bigl(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}\bigr) \] with $C_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k>0$, where $r_k(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression.
MAIN STATEMENTS: [Quasipolynomial inverse theorem] Fix an integer $s\ge1$. Let $p\ge2$. A unit-bounded function on an interval whose $U^{s+1}$ norm is at least $e^{-p}$ correlates by at least $\mathcal B(p)^{-1}$ with a unit-bounded degree-$s$ niltest of complexity $\mathcal P(p)$. The same conclusion holds on integer boxes and on products of cyclic groups, with the following dimension convention: for every fixed $A\ge1$, dimension $n\le(2+p)^A$ is permitted, and the constants and polynomial exponents may depend | [Shift comparison] For fixed $d\geq1$ and $0<\epsilon<1$, there is a constant $C=C(d,\epsilon)$ such that the following holds. Suppose that $p\geq2$, $N\geq\exp((2+p)^C)$ is odd, and $0\leq f,g,J\leq e^p$. Set $P=(2+p)^C$. If \begin{equation} \E_n(f-g)(n)T(n)\leq e^{-P} \qquad(T\in\mathcal T_d(P)), \end{equation} then there is a set $E\subseteq G$, depending on $f,g,J$, with $|E|\leq e^{-p}N$, such that \begin{equation} \E_n\bigl(f-(1+\epsilon)g\bigr)(n)J(n+h)T'(n)\leq e^{-p} \qquad(h\notin E,\  | [Degree-one shift comparison] Theorem~ holds for $d=1$.
